title: Enchanted Light Mixing Table
description: The user arranges a glass hurricane candle holder and a translucent teacup on a circular table, filling each vessel with colored light energy. By pouring light between vessels, adjusting hue and intensity, and using undo/redo, the user must mix and conserve a fixed total luminance budget across both objects to match a target color palette displayed on a floating card.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap/CDN) implementing an interactive light-mixing puzzle. Load GlassHurricaneCandleHolder.glb and DiffuseTransmissionTeacup.glb using GLTFLoader, placing them on a circular wooden table mesh at positions (-1.2, 0, 0) and (1.2, 0, 0). Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 5) with OrbitControls. Add an HDR-style environment using PMREMGenerator with a neutral studio preset, plus a warm AmbientLight(0xffeedd, 0.3) and a DirectionalLight from above. Each vessel contains a glowing PointLight representing its stored light energy. Implement a fixed total luminance budget of 6.0 units shared across both vessels (conservation law). The UI panel on the left shows: (1) a hue wheel for each vessel to set its PointLight color, (2) an intensity slider per vessel (0-6 range, but combined cannot exceed 6.0 — adjusting one auto-clamps the other), (3) a 'Pour' button that transfers 0.5 units from the selected source vessel to the other with a particle animation arc between them, (4) Undo and Redo buttons tracking all state changes in a history stack (color, intensity per vessel). Clicking a vessel selects it (outline via post-processing or emissive highlight). A floating target card mesh shows two color swatches the user must match within a tolerance of deltaE < 15 in LAB space. Display a match percentage indicator per vessel. The pour animation should spawn 8 small emissive spheres traveling a bezier arc from source to target over 0.6 seconds. Apply MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission=0.9 and roughness=0.05 to both loaded models for realistic glass appearance. When both vessels match their targets, play a success sparkle particle burst. Ensure at least 10-14 interaction steps are needed: selecting vessels, adjusting hues, transferring light, undoing mistakes, and fine-tuning intensities under the conservation constraint.
